findings.title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (a darker shade suitable for bold usernames in light themes). The conversion replaced it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, which makes the light-theme branch `lightness: 70%` instead of 30%. The PR's stated intent is to add a dark-theme branch while preserving the existing light-theme appearance, so the light branch's `70%` is wrong: it should be `30%`. In light themes, embedded-post meta-data usernames will visibly appear much lighter than before.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.group-member-info .name)
findings.body: In `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The conversion became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so the light-theme branch now uses `lightness: 50%` instead of the original `30%`. The neighbouring `.group-member-info .title` selector in the same block kept its `50%` lightness correctly; only `.name` got its first-argument lightness changed, making the two siblings inconsistently colored and clearly different from before in light themes.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.group-member-info .name)
findings.body: In `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should have stayed at `30%` (as the sibling `.group-member-info .title` did) but was changed to `50%`, producing a lighter, visibly different color in light themes and breaking the relative contrast between `.name` and `.title` that the original defined.

findings.title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.topic-map h3)
findings.body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, making the light-theme branch `50%` instead of `20%`. The corresponding desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` for the same `.topic-map h3`) correctly preserves `lightness: 20%` in the light branch and `80%` in the dark branch, so this is an inconsistency between desktop and mobile and an unintended visual change in light themes: topic-map headings will appear much lighter on mobile.

findings.title: Inverted lightness on light-theme branch (.custom-message-length)
findings.body: In `.custom-message-length`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The conversion became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping the light/dark arguments. The light-theme branch is now `lightness: 30%` (the dark shade), and the dark-theme branch is `lightness: 70%` (the light shade) — the exact opposite of every other conversion in this PR. The matching desktop rule in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly uses `70%` / `30%`. In light themes on mobile, the custom-message hint text will appear as a dark shade instead of the intended lighter grey, hurting readability.
